# Purpose and provenance

This notebook explains the completed Information Visualization reanalysis and
displays its actual outputs. It is adapted from the local classroom notebook
`Genomics/gb_RNAseq_student.Rmd`; the original file is unchanged. Source data:
[Narain et al., 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41398-024-03100-w),
[GIN dataset](https://doi.gin.g-node.org/10.12751/g-node.jj57l9/).
This is not an exact reproduction of the paper's statistical workflow.

The default render reads saved results. To refit, first run
`python scripts/prepare_inputs.py`, then render with `params=list(recompute=TRUE)`.
The analysis requires raw integer counts, not the author-normalized tables.

```{r optional-recompute}
if (isTRUE(params$recompute)) source('analysis/run_analysis.R')
```

# Metadata decisions

93 included tissues represent 47 animals. Source and analysis identifiers are
kept separately. C01_E1 is ZT4, following the corrected raw filenames. A15_A
brain-region labels are swapped once in analysis metadata: full-gene matching
to the author's normalized tables reconstructs the opposite source count file
to floating-point precision. Author exclusions are L1R-E05_5, S1R-E05_5 and
L2S-E05_1. No additional outcome-driven exclusions were applied.

```{r sample-design}
samples <- read.csv('results/samples.csv')
stopifnot(nrow(samples)==93, !anyDuplicated(samples$sample_id_analysis))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(xtabs(~region+zt+phenotype,samples)))
```

# Classroom steps and explicit adaptations

The lesson's core pipeline is retained: count filtering, DESeq2 negative-binomial
models, explicit pairwise contrasts, annotated genes, and GO overrepresentation.
Because these data already contain counts, BAM counting is unnecessary.

- Filtering: retain a gene if any phenotype's median raw count is at least 10
  within a region/time stratum.
- Normalization: DESeq2 median ratios estimated jointly across times within
  each region; the same factors feed expression profiles and stratum models.
- Models: eight independent `~ phenotype` fits using all three groups; three
  explicit contrasts per fit. There is no cross-region or interaction test.
- Effects: unshrunken log2 fold changes, positive for the first named phenotype.
- Default exploration: p-adj < .05 and absolute log2FC > .5, unlike the classroom
  defaults .1 / 1. Independent filtering remains fixed at alpha=.05.
- QC: PCA on log2 normalized counts for 500 variable genes; explicitly not VST.
- GO: mouse OrgDb in place of Arabidopsis TAIR; Python implements one-sided
  hypergeometric/BH with finite-padj GO-mapped background, instead of claiming
  execution of clusterProfiler. This InfoVis deliverable does not add GSEA.

# Results and meaningful checks

```{r actual-results}
overview <- read.csv('results/overview.csv')
overview$DEGs <- overview$up+overview$down
knitr::kable(overview[,c('region','zt','contrast','tested_genes','unavailable_padj','DEGs','n_group1','n_group2')])
validation <- read.csv('audit/model_validation.csv')
stopifnot(nrow(overview)==24,all(validation$reverse_contrast_pass))
knitr::kable(validation)
```

Resilient/control has 779 passing genes in SCN ZT16 and 225 in Hb ZT16 in this
reanalysis. That pattern does not itself establish a phenotype-by-time
interaction. Counts across contexts depend on power and the tested universe.
Missing p-values and adjusted p-values remain NA; they are not evidence for
zero effects. Source-to-export validation independently reconstructs filters,
all normalized counts, exported contrast precision and GO p-values/BH adjustment.

```{r example-candidates}
r <- read.csv('results/contrasts/SCN_zt16_resilient_vs_control.csv')
knitr::kable(head(r[order(r$padj),c('ensembl_id','symbol','log2FoldChange','padj')],10),digits=7)
```

# GO annotation and enrichment

GOALL BP memberships include ancestor terms. Background is the GO-mapped genes
with finite adjusted p-values in a contrast. Eligible terms have 10–500 background
genes. All eligible terms, including zero overlaps, enter BH correction. The
network is annotation-only if no term passes q<.05. Default enrichment does not
change when the website's exploration cutoffs change.

```{r go-results}
go <- read.csv('results/go_enrichment_all.csv')
g <- subset(go,context=='SCN_zt16_resilient_vs_control')
knitr::kable(head(g[order(g$padj),c('id','name','overlap_count','background_size','foreground_size','padj')],10),digits=10)
knitr::kable(read.csv('results/annotation_metadata.csv'))
```

# Reproducibility and limitations

The analysis scripts, hashes, exported values and browser acceptance checks
are included. The all-zero gene, no-DEG and no-GO states are tested explicitly.
Different sampling times contain different animals. Group means are descriptive;
this dataset is small, male-only and bulk tissue, with possible unmodeled batch
effects. Team scientific review and a human usability study remain separate
from automated validation. OpenAI Codex assisted implementation and documentation;
team members must understand and revise submitted work (see AI_USAGE.md).

```{r actual-session, echo=FALSE}
cat(paste(readLines('results/session_info.txt'),collapse='\n'))
```
